The test `testIssue631()` expects the RegulaFalsiSolver to throw a ConvergenceException when trying to find a root of the function f(x) = exp(x) - pi^3 in the interval [1, 10] within a large number of iterations (3624).

The failure suggests that the solver either does not throw the expected exception or incorrectly finds a root.

The test function is strictly positive at the endpoints (exp(1) and exp(10) are both larger than pi^3, but pi^3 is approximately 31, so exp(1) ~ 2.7 < 31, exp(10) ~ 22026 > 31), so the root should exist within the interval since the function will cross zero somewhere in between.

The RegulaFalsiSolver constructor just calls its superclass constructor with a default absolute accuracy and the method enum Method.REGULA_FALSI.

The doSolve method we tried to get is abstract in BaseAbstractUnivariateRealSolver, so the actual solver logic might be implemented in a class nearer to RegulaFalsiSolver or in itself but named differently.

The error message or current bug report snippet is truncated so it is not fully clear why the failure happens.

There could be an issue in bracketing check (whether the initial interval does bracket a root) or in the iteration process of the solver itself, possibly causing it not to converge or throw an exception as expected.
